project: Automatos AI Platform — PRD-224 The Ticket Lane: Auto as Line Manager (Auto-as-Manager wave, chain 2/6)

userStories.title: [CRITICAL] Ambiguous agent-name resolution silently dispatches to the WRONG agent instead of asking in-thread
userStories.description: REVIEW FINDING (chain 2/6 adversarial review + code-reviewer, both independent). consumers/chatbot/auto.py:909-926 _match_roster_agent does exact-match first, then a bidirectional substring fallback ('if an in target or target in an: return a.id, a.name') that returns on the FIRST hit with NO ambiguity check. The roster source _active_agents (auto.py:886-901) has NO order_by, so when >1 agent substring-matches, which one wins is whatever order Postgres returns (nondeterministic). Concrete failure: workspace has active agents 'Jim Whitfield' and 'Jimmy Cross'; user says 'Have Jim send the invoice reminder now'; classifier extracts target_agent='Jim'; no exact match, so the contains loop fires and BOTH match ('jim' is a prefix of 'jimmy') — the first row returned silently becomes target_agent_name, resolved=True, and build_assign_directive (auto.py:89-128) tells Auto to file+start the ticket for the wrong agent, immediately (in_progress) and auto-supervised, with zero user visibility. create_board_task (handlers_board_tasks.py:85-90) then faithfully assigns the real ticket to that wrong agent by exact name. This directly violates the baked decision + PRD Wave-1 AC 'Ambiguous/unknown agent name -> Auto asks in-thread rather than guessing' (docs/PRDS/PRD-224-AUTO-TICKET-LANE.md:78) and the function's own docstring claim 'NEVER a fuzzy best-guess'. Short agent names ('Ops','AI') compound it — they substring-match almost any longer target. NOT cross-workspace (roster filters workspace_id; cache key is workspace-prefixed) and a stale cached id is re-verified at tool time — the defect is specifically the missing ambiguity check on the within-workspace contains-match. Existing coverage test_match_roster_contains_possessive (tests/test_prd224_assign_lane.py:151-154) only exercises a SINGLE-agent roster, so the multi-match case is untested. Fix direction: when the exact-match loop misses AND the contains check yields other-than-exactly-one candidate (0 or >=2), return (None, None) so the turn takes the ask-in-thread path — never a first-of-many pick.
acceptanceCriteria: DONE — _match_roster_agent (auto.py): exact-name loop UNCHANGED (a single exact hit still resolves first). When exact misses, the contains fallback now collects EVERY match into a dict keyed by agent id and resolves ONLY when len(matches)==1 (exactly one distinct agent); 0 or ≥2 distinct matches return (None, None). Order-independent (dict-by-id, never first-row), so target_agent_id stays None and apply_assign_bias/build_assign_directive take the resolved=False ask-in-thread branch.

DONE — tests/test_prd224_assign_lane.py +5: test_match_roster_ambiguous_contains_asks_not_guesses ('Jim' vs 'Jim Whitfield'+'Jimmy Cross' → (None,None)); _ambiguous_is_order_independent (both roster orders → None); _two_short_names_are_ambiguous ('AI Ops' vs 'Ops'/'AI'); _single_contains_still_resolves_amid_others ('my accountant agent' → (7,'Accountant') amid a Researcher); _ambiguous_match_drives_ask_in_thread_directive (platform_list_agents + 'Do NOT guess or auto-pick'). userStories.title: [CRITICAL] ASSIGN immediate-start races the board dispatcher — the same ticket can EXECUTE twice
userStories.description: REVIEW FINDING (chain 2/6 adversarial review + code-reviewer, both independent). The ASSIGN imperative-default path (the baked 'START IMMEDIATELY' case) has Auto do two back-to-back tool calls per build_assign_directive (auto.py:99-119): (1) platform_create_task (lands status='assigned' since the agent resolved and no explicit status is passed — handlers_board_tasks.py:98) then (2) platform_update_task_status -> 'in_progress'. US-001's NEW _notify_dispatch_safe on create (handlers_board_tasks.py:164-165, fired by _is_dispatch_claimable when assigned+agent) wakes board_dispatcher.run_dispatch_loop (started in main.py:585) at sub-second LISTEN/NOTIFY latency; the dispatcher's claim_tasks (services/board_dispatcher.py:64-181, FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) flips the row to in_progress and calls _launch_task_execution (board_dispatcher.py:474) = launch #1. Auto's step-2 update_board_task_status then launches AGAIN: the inline trigger at handlers_board_tasks.py:421 ('if new_status == in_progress and task.assigned_agent_id: _launch_task_execution(...)') has NO old_status/lease guard, so it re-launches even though the dispatcher already claimed the row = launch #2. Both call AgentFactory.execute_with_prompt concurrently for the same task_id — the agent's REAL side effects (emails, external API calls, writes) run twice; the only mutual-exclusion is the terminal status-write at the end (second finisher sees status != in_progress and skips its DB write), which MASKS the double-run on the board. The codebase already knows this guard is required: run_task_now (api/board_tasks.py:871) does 'if task.status == in_progress: raise 409' before calling the shared _redispatch_task, whose docstring even states 'Caller guarantees the task is not already in_progress' — that guard is simply absent on the chat-side update path. SAME-CLASS second site: watch_actions.run_board_task_action (services/watch_actions.py) calls _redispatch_task with no in-progress re-check (narrower window — the ticker only reaches it after a terminal read — but a human 'Run Now' or other restart between the terminal read and the decider's rerun re-opens it). This is the default 'start now' path, not an edge case. Fix direction: make the transition-to-in_progress launch conditional on the prior status (skip the launch when the row is already in_progress, mirroring run_task_now's 409/claim_tasks idiom), and add the same in-progress guard to run_board_task_action before _redispatch_task.
acceptanceCriteria: DONE — update_board_task_status (handlers_board_tasks.py): the inline _launch_task_execution now fires only when new_status=='in_progress' AND assigned agent AND old_status!='in_progress' (old_status is captured at the read). By the time Auto's back-to-back status write runs, board_dispatcher.claim_tasks has usually already claimed the row (flipping it to in_progress) — the guard mirrors the Run-Now route's own check at api/board_tasks.py:871, so a write of in_progress onto an already-in_progress row launches ZERO extra executions. triggered_execution now returns the real 'launched' flag (honest, no longer claims a launch it skipped).

userStories.title: [MEDIUM] ASSIGN directive scripts the 'supervised' confirmation unconditionally — dishonest when AUTO_TICKET_WATCH is off / no watch attached
userStories.description: REVIEW FINDING (chain 2/6 adversarial review; related strand flagged by code-reviewer). build_assign_directive (auto.py:99-119) always appends 'Confirm ... that it is {started|queued} and supervised — you will report back here' for a resolved-agent ASSIGN. But the supervision is decided LATER in the handler: US-005 supports a not-supervised outcome — when config.AUTO_TICKET_WATCH is off, create_board_task returns supervised=False and supervision='not supervised (AUTO_TICKET_WATCH is off)' (handlers_board_tasks.py:183-185) — and the watch can also legitimately fail to attach (dial off, or auto_create_ticket_watch returns None). The directive is built at api/chat.py dispatch time and never consults the dial, so it deterministically instructs Auto to CLAIM supervision even in the dial-off case, contradicting the tool result and the standing 'loud, honest visible activation' feedback (the whole point of the confirmation line). Fix direction: the directive must not hardcode a 'supervised' assertion; it must instruct Auto to state supervision status FROM the platform_create_task result's supervised/supervision fields, so the dial-off case confirms honestly (no false 'I will report back here').
acceptanceCriteria: build_assign_directive output no longer contains an unconditional 'supervised — you will report back here' assertion; the confirmation step instructs Auto to report supervision per the platform_create_task result (the supervised / supervision fields), so an AUTO_TICKET_WATCH-off ticket is not described as supervised.

A test asserts the directive string does not unconditionally assert supervision and references the create result's supervision status; existing ASSIGN-directive tests (start / queued / ask-in-thread) stay green.
